# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC: 80 A Burst Thermal/Loss Model and Bidirectional DShot600 Allocation

## 0. Scope and Assumptions

I have no prior context for "Job #4", so every input parameter below is stated explicitly. Replace each one with datasheet and layout values before using any result.

**Architecture correction:** In a 4-in-1 stack, the STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and only *commands* the ESC over DShot. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by the ESC's own MCU (typically AT32F421, STM32G071 or EFM8 running AM32/BLHeli). The loss model below applies to the ESC power stage. The DMA/timer model applies to the H743.

| Parameter | Symbol | Assumed value |
|---|---|---|
| Battery | V_bus | 6S, 25.2 V max (worst case for switching) |
| Burst phase current per motor | I_m | 80 A |
| MOSFET | — | 40 V, DFN3.3×3, 1 FET per switch (6 per motor, 24 total) |
| R_DS(on) at 25 °C / at T_j = 125 °C | R_25 / R_hot | 1.2 mΩ / ≈1.9 mΩ (tempco factor ≈1.6) |
| Rise + fall time | t_r + t_f | 15 + 15 ns |
| Dead time | t_dt | 200 ns per edge |
| Body-diode forward voltage | V_f | 0.8 V |
| Reverse-recovery charge / output charge | Q_rr / Q_oss | 40 nC / 25 nC |
| Total gate charge / gate voltage | Q_g / V_GS | 40 nC / 10 V |
| PWM frequency | f_sw | 48 kHz, complementary (synchronous rectification) |
| Commutation | — | Trapezoidal, 120° |
| Board | — | 20×20 mm, 6-layer, 2 oz outer copper |

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model (80 A Burst)

With 120° trapezoidal commutation, exactly two phases carry current at any instant: one high-side path and one low-side path.

With synchronous rectification, the PWM-off interval freewheels through the complementary FET of the same leg. So the conducting resistance is always about 2·R_DS(on), independent of duty cycle.

**Instantaneous conduction loss per motor:**

$$P_{cond,motor} = 2\,I_m^2\,R_{DS(on)}(T_j)$$

**Temperature dependence:**

$$R_{DS(on)}(T_j) = R_{25}\left[1+\alpha(T_j-25)\right],\quad \alpha \approx 0.006\ \text{K}^{-1}$$

**Per-FET average.** Each switch position conducts for one third of the electrical period:

$$I_{rms,FET} = I_m\sqrt{1/3} = 46.2\ \text{A},\qquad P_{cond,FET}=I_{rms,FET}^2 R_{DS(on)}$$

**Numbers:**

| Quantity | At 25 °C | At T_j = 125 °C |
|---|---|---|
| P_cond per FET | 2.56 W | **4.05 W** |
| P_cond per motor (×6) | 15.4 W | **24.3 W** |

**Copper and bus losses.** Assume about 0.25 mΩ of trace, via and pad resistance in each current path, two paths per motor:

$$P_{Cu} \approx 2\cdot 80^2 \cdot 0.25\,\text{m}\Omega \approx 3.2\ \text{W per motor}$$

**Positive feedback.** Because R_DS(on) rises with T_j, conduction loss and temperature reinforce each other. The fixed-point equation is:

$$T_j = T_a + R_{th}\cdot P(T_j)$$

It has no stable solution if:

$$R_{th}\cdot \frac{\partial P}{\partial T_j} = R_{th}\cdot 2I_m^2 R_{25}\alpha \geq 1$$

That is thermal runaway, and it is the real burst limiter (see Section 3).

---

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

Only the PWM-modulated leg switches; the other conducting leg is static during a 60° sector. Hard switching occurs on the active FET.

| Component | Formula | Per motor at 80 A, 25.2 V |
|---|---|---|
| V–I overlap | ½·V·I·(t_r + t_f)·f_sw = ½·25.2·80·30 ns·48 k | **1.45 W** |
| Dead-time body-diode conduction | V_f·I·(2·t_dt)·f_sw = 0.8·80·400 ns·48 k | **1.23 W** |
| Reverse recovery | Q_rr·V·f_sw = 40 nC·25.2·48 k | 0.05 W |
| C_oss (Q_oss) | Q_oss·V·f_sw | 0.03 W |
| Gate drive (driver loss, 2 FETs) | 2·Q_g·V_GS·f_sw | 0.04 W |
| **Total switching-related** | | **≈2.8 W** |

**Design implications:**
- Dead-time loss is about as large as the overlap loss. Cutting t_dt from 200 ns to 100 ns saves about 0.6 W per motor. Only do this if you verify there is no shoot-through over temperature.
- Overlap loss scales linearly with f_sw. At 24 kHz it is about 0.7 W. However, the per-motor total is roughly 89% conduction-dominated at 80 A, so lowering f_sw buys little; reducing R_DS(on) buys a lot.

## 3. Total Loss and Thermal Model

### 3.1 Loss budget at 80 A burst, T_j = 125 °C

| Item | Per motor | Board (×4) |
|---|---|---|
| Conduction | 24.3 W | 97.2 W |
| Switching + dead-time | 2.8 W | 11.2 W |
| Copper / connectors | 3.2 W | 12.8 W |
| **Total** | **≈30 W** | **≈121 W** |

### 3.2 Steady-state check (proves "burst only")

Assume a convection coefficient of h ≈ 100 W/m²K in prop-wash. The board has two exposed faces:

$$A = 2\times(0.02)^2 = 8\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2,\qquad R_{th,sa}=\frac{1}{hA}=12.5\ \text{K/W}$$

$$\Delta T_{ss}=121\times 12.5 \approx 1500\ \text{K}$$

**Conclusion: 80 A per motor is not survivable continuously on a 20×20 board.** It is only survivable as a short transient bounded by thermal mass.
